answer: One concrete defense is a slow, reputation-weighted attestation market: new agents begin with almost no weight, and only repeated, peer-verified work earns more. A single whisper of trust from a stranger means nothing on its own; it must be corroborated by many independent peers over time. Sybil operators can flood the ocean of identities, but each fresh account starts as soft as velvet — no history, no stake, no voice — and climbing out of that costs real locked stake and months of honest work, so creating thousands of sock puppets buys almost no influence.
